Permissible Activities for Bank Holding Companies
paragraphs: Byline Bancorp, Inc., headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, is a bank holding company. We conduct all our business activities through our subsidiary, Byline Bank, a full service commercial bank, and Byline Bank's subsidiaries. The words "the Company," "we," "Byline," "our" and "us" refer to Byline Bancorp, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries, unless we indicate otherwise.

We offer a broad range of banking products and services to small and medium sized businesses, commercial real estate and financial sponsors and to consumers who generally live or work near our branches. We also offer online account opening to consumer and business customers through our website and provide trust and wealth management services to our customers. In addition to our traditional commercial banking business, we provide small ticket equipment leasing solutions through Byline Financial Group, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Byline Bank, headquartered in Bannockburn, Illinois with sales offices in Illinois, and sales representatives in Illinois and New York. We participate in U.S. government guaranteed lending programs and originate U.S. government guaranteed loans. Byline Bank was the tenth most active originator of SBA 7(a) loans in the country and the most active SBA 7(a) lender in Illinois, as reported by the SBA for its fiscal year ended September 30, 2025. As of December 31, 2025, we had consolidated total assets of $9.7 billion, total gross loans and leases outstanding of $7.5 billion, total deposits of $7.6 billion, and total stockholders' equity of $1.3 billion.

As part of our strategic plan, we explore potential opportunities for expansion in our primary and adjacent market areas through organic growth and the acquisition of financial institutions, branches, and non-banking organizations. Our aspiration to be the preeminent commercial bank in Chicago drives our focus on market expansion, deepening client relationships, and fostering a strong-cross sell culture to enhance retention and revenue diversification. We also prioritize process improvement and productivity enhancements, leveraging technology and best practices to improve efficiency, scalability, and the overall customer experience, all with commitment to disciplined oversight and aligned risk practices.

We believe our local presence and our scale are essential to the continued growth of our deposit base. Small businesses are a significant source of low-cost deposits and represent opportunities for future growth. We believe our small business customers value our ability to provide convenience and access to local, responsive decision makers. As of December 31, 2025, commercial deposits accounted for 43.0% of total deposits and were 85.1% of non-interest bearing deposits. Commercial accounts generally have higher deposit balances and transaction volumes than individual deposit accounts.

Our ability to originate loans and leases across a range of industries and product types helps us maintain a diversified loan and lease portfolio across various sectors, including commercial and industrial lending, leasing, U.S. government guaranteed loans and real estate loans, allowing us to efficiently manage our credit exposures and capitalize on more lending opportunities. We have continued to enhance our product and lending capabilities with the addition of experienced lending teams hired from larger banks.
The following charts outline the composition of our loan and lease and deposit portfolios as of December 31, 2025:

Our ability to engage in certain merger or acquisition transactions depends on a number of factors, including opportunities in our market areas, access to capital, our bank regulators' views at the time as to the capital levels, quality of management and our overall financial condition, in addition to their assessment of a variety of other factors, including our compliance with laws and regulations. We have successfully completed a number of strategic acquisitions since our recapitalization in 2013, which include:
Oak Park River Forest Bankshares, Inc. 2018
Ridgestone Financial Services, Inc. 2014 Baytree Leasing Company LLC

On April 1, 2025, we completed our acquisition of First Security Bancorp, Inc., a Delaware corporation ("First Security Bancorp"), and First Security Bancorp's wholly-owned bank subsidiary, First Security Trust and Savings Bank ("First Security'), an Illinois chartered bank (collectively "First Security acquisition" or "acquisition of First Security"). Refer to Note 3—Acquisition of a Business contained within Part II, Item 8, Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements of this document.

The primary market in which we operate is the Chicago metropolitan area, and our 44 branch network in this area is our core distribution channel. We take advantage of our focused footprint and deep-rooted relationships to target local customers with a diversified product offering.

Our local branch network enables us to gather low cost deposits, promote the Byline brand and customer loyalty, originate loans, leases and other products and maintain relationships with our customers through regular community involvement. We believe our branch network is fundamental to our ability to achieve successful customer outreach in line with our culture, which promotes high touch engagement with our customers and proactive solutions.

While our branch network continues to be our primary delivery channel, we understand the evolving banking environment requires digital interaction to keep pace with our customers' needs. We continually perform strategic reviews of our branch network and our existing banking footprint. With technology improvements and changes to customers' banking preferences, we regularly examine both branch growth and consolidation potential, including customer usage, branch profitability, services provided, markets served and proximity to other locations.

Since our recapitalization in June 2013, our branch network has been reduced from 88 to 45, including 24 branches added through acquisition. During 2025, one branch was closed and consolidated into existing branch locations, and one leased branch location was assumed as part of the First Security acquisition and was subsequently closed after acquisition.

headings: Our business depends on our ability to successfully manage credit risk.
We may underestimate the credit losses inherent in our loan and lease portfolio and have credit losses in excess of the amount we provide for loan and lease losses.
Our business is subject to interest rate risk and fluctuations in interest rates may adversely affect our earnings.
We depend on the accuracy and completeness of information about customers and counterparties.
The value of the financial instruments we own may decline in the future.
A lack of liquidity could affect operations and jeopardize our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
Our liquidity is dependent on dividends from Byline Bank.
We may need to raise additional capital in the future, and such capital may not be available when needed or at all.
We may not be able to implement our growth strategy or manage costs effectively, resulting in lower earnings or profitability.
New lines of business, products, product enhancements or services and technologies may subject us to additional risks.
Our business may be adversely affected by conditions in the financial markets and economic conditions generally.
Our business is significantly dependent on the real estate markets in which we operate, as a significant percentage of our loan portfolio is secured by real estate.
AI and our ability to implement and leverage AI to deliver new products and services to our customers present competitive risks.
The recognition of gains on the sale of loans and servicing asset valuations reflects certain assumptions.
Our accounting estimates and risk management processes and controls rely on analytical and forecasting techniques and models and assumptions, which may not accurately predict future events.

Our goodwill may become impaired, which may adversely impact our results of operations and financial condition and may limit Byline Bank's ability to pay dividends to us, thereby causing liquidity issues.
Our ability to recognize the benefits of deferred tax assets is dependent on future cash flows and taxable income.
Certain activities are restricted due to commitments entered into with the FRB by us and our foreign national stockholders.
Monetary policies and regulations of the FRB could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.

We are subject to numerous laws designed to protect consumers, including the Community Reinvestment Act and fair lending laws, and failure to comply with these laws could lead to a wide variety of sanctions.
Non-compliance with the USA PATRIOT Act, the Bank Secrecy Act or other laws and regulations could result in fines or sanctions against us.

Regulations relating to privacy, information security, and data protection could increase our costs, affect or limit how we collect and use personal information, and adversely affect our business opportunities.

There is uncertainty surrounding the potential legal, regulatory and policy changes by the presidential administration in the United States that may directly affect financial institutions and the global economy.
Our consolidated assets are expected to exceed $10 billion, which may result in increased regulation and supervision of Byline Bank and may also result in increased costs and/or reduced revenue.
paragraphs: The material risks and uncertainties that management believes affect us are described below. You should carefully consider these risks, together with all of the information included herein. Any of the following risks, as well as risks that we do not know or currently deem immaterial, could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, or results of operations.

The operation of our business requires us to manage credit risk. As a lender, we are exposed to the risk that our borrowers may be unable to repay their loans and leases according to their terms, and that the collateral securing repayment of their loans or leases, if any, may not be sufficient to ensure repayment. In addition, there are risks inherent in making any loan or lease, including risks with respect to the period of time over which the loan or lease may be repaid, risks relating to proper loan or lease underwriting, risks resulting from changes in economic and industry conditions and risks inherent in dealing with individual borrowers, including the risk that a borrower may not provide information to us about its business in a timely manner, and/or may present inaccurate or incomplete information to us, and risks relating to the value of collateral. In order to manage credit risk successfully, we must, among other things, maintain disciplined and prudent underwriting standards. The weakening of these standards for any reason, a lack of discipline or diligence in underwriting and monitoring loans and leases, the inability to adequately adapt policies and procedures to changes in economic or any other conditions affecting borrowers and the quality of our loan and lease portfolio, may result in defaults, foreclosures and additional charge-offs and may necessitate that we significantly increase our allowance for credit losses - loans and leases, each of which could adversely affect our net income. As a result, our inability to successfully manage credit risk could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, or results of operations.

The credit quality of our loan and lease portfolio can have a significant impact on our earnings. We maintain an allowance for credit losses, which is a reserve established through a provision charged to expense representing management's estimate of current expected credit losses. The allowance, in the judgment of management, is necessary to reserve for current expected losses and risks inherent in our loan and lease portfolio. The level of the allowance reflects management's continuing evaluation of specific credit risks; the quality of the portfolio; the value of the underlying collateral; the level of non-accruing loans and leases; current expected losses inherent in the portfolio; and economic, political, and regulatory conditions. Management estimates the allowance balance using relevant available information from internal and external sources relating to past events, current conditions, and reasonable and supportable forecasts, which could increase the subjectivity of the calculation. This process, which is critical to our financial results and condition, requires difficult, subjective and complex judgments. In accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America ("GAAP") for business combination accounting, the loans acquired through subsequent bank acquisitions are recorded at their estimated fair value, and an allowance for credit losses associated with those loans also recorded.

Although we believe our allowance for credit losses is adequate to absorb current expected losses in our loan and lease portfolio, it may not be sufficient. We could sustain credit losses that are significantly higher than the amount of our allowance as a result of a variety of reasons, such as changes in economic conditions affecting borrowers, new information and other factors within and outside our control. If real estate values were to decline or if economic conditions in our markets were to deteriorate unexpectedly, additional losses not incorporated in the existing allowance might occur. Losses in excess of the existing allowance will reduce our net income and could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, or results of operations. A severe downturn in the economy generally, in our markets specifically, or affecting the business and assets of individual customers, would generate increased charge-offs and a need for higher provision for credit losses.

We may also be required to take additional provisions for credit losses in the future to further supplement the allowance due to requirements by our banking regulators. Bank regulatory agencies periodically review our allowance, the policies and procedures we use to determine the level of the allowance and the value attributed to non-performing loans or to real estate acquired through foreclosure. Such regulatory agencies may require us to make further provisions or recognize future charge-offs. Further, charge-offs in future periods that exceed the allowance would require an increase to the allowance.

Any increases in our provision for credit losses will result in a decrease in net income and may reduce retained earnings and capital and, therefore, have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

paragraphs: Our results of operations depend substantially on net interest income, which is the difference between interest income on interest-earning assets, consisting primarily of interest income on loans and lease receivables, including accretion income on loans, investment securities and other short-term investments, and interest expense on interest-bearing liabilities, consisting primarily of deposits and borrowings. Our results of operations are also dependent upon our generation of non-interest income, consisting primarily of income from fees and service charges on deposits, loan servicing revenue, wealth management and trust income, ATM and interchange fees, and net gains on sales of investment securities and loans. Other factors contributing to our results of operations include our provisions for credit losses, provision for income taxes, and non-interest expenses, such as salaries and employee benefits, occupancy and equipment expenses, data processing expenses, and other miscellaneous operating costs.

The Company's financial condition, operating results, and liquidity during 2025 were impacted by record revenues driven by growth in the loan and lease portfolio and lower rates paid on deposits, our acquisition of First Security, and actions taken to continue to strengthen the balance sheet.

We reported consolidated net income of $130.1 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to net income of $120.8 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, an increase of $9.3 million, or 7.7%. The increase in net income was attributable to a $37.3 million increase in net interest income, and a $2.1 million increase in non-interest income, offset by a $18.1 million increase in non-interest expense, a $9.1 million increase in provision for credit losses, and a $2.9 million increase in provision for income taxes. For the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, our earnings per basic share were $2.90 and $2.78, and per diluted share were $2.89 and $2.75, respectively. Our results of operations for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, produced an annual return on average assets of 1.36% and 1.31% and a return on average stockholders' equity of 10.86% and 11.61%, respectively.

Total assets were $9.7 billion as of December 31, 2025, an increase of $156.1 million or 1.6%, compared to $9.5 billion as of December 31, 2024. Total deposits were $7.6 billion as of December 31, 2025, an increase $188.8 million or 2.5%, from $7.5 billion as of December 31, 2024. Total borrowings and other liabilities were $737.3 million at December 31, 2025, a decrease of $209.1 million or 22.1%, from $946.4 million as of December 31, 2024. Total stockholders' equity as of December 31, 2025 was $1.3 billion, an increase of $176.4 million or 16.2%, compared to $1.1 billion as of December 31, 2024. Dividends declared on common shares were $18.2 million and $15.9 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. Dividends paid on common shares were $18.2 million and $15.8 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.

paragraphs: Byline Bancorp, Inc., 著冊總部位於美國伊利諾州芝加哥，為一家銀行控股公司。我們所有業務活動均透過我們的子公司 Byline Bank，一家提供全面商業銀行服務的銀行，以及 Byline Bank 的子公司進行。文中 "the Company," "we," "Byline," "our" 和 "us" 係指 Byline Bancorp, Inc. 及其合併子公司，除非我們另有說明。

我們為小型及中型企業、商業不動產及財務機構，以及一般居住或工作在本行分行附近的消費者，提供廣泛的銀行產品與服務。我們亦透過網站為消費者與企業客戶提供網上開戶服務，並為客戶提供信託與資產管理服務。除了傳統的商業銀行業務外，我們透過 Byline Financial Group，一家位於伊利諾州 Bannockburn 的 Byline Bank 全資子公司，提供小額設備租賃解決方案，並在伊利諾州設有銷售辦事處，以及在伊利諾州與紐約設有銷售代表。我們參與美國政府擔保貸款計劃，並發放美國政府擔保貸款。根據美國小企業管理局（SBA）於其財務年度截至 2025 年 9 月 30 日的報告，Byline Bank 為美國第十大 SBA 7(a) 貸款發放機構，並為伊利諾州最活躍的 SBA 7(a) 貸款機構。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們合併總資產為 9.7 十億美元，總放款與租賃餘額為 7.5 十億美元，總存款為 7.6 十億美元，總股東權益為 1.3 十億美元。
根據我們的戰略計畫，我們探討在主要及鄰近市場地區透過內生成長與收購金融機構、分行及非銀行組織，尋求潛在擴張機會。我們希望成為芝加哥首屈一指的商業銀行，這驅動我們專注於市場擴張、深化客戶關係，並培養強大的交叉銷售文化，以提升客戶留存與收入多元化。我們亦優先考量流程改善與生產力提升，運用科技與最佳實務以提高效率、可擴展性與整體客戶體驗，並秉持嚴謹的監督與風險管理實踐。
我們相信本地化存在與規模是我們存款基礎持續成長的關鍵。小型企業是低成本存款的重要來源，並代表未來成長的機會。我們相信小型企業客戶看重我們能提供便利與接近本地、靈活決策者的服務能力。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，商業存款佔總存款的 43.0%，且為非利息存款的 85.1%。商業帳戶通常具有較高的存款餘額與交易量，較個人存款帳戶為高。
我們能跨多個產業與產品類型發放貸款與租賃，有助於我們維持一個分散於不同產業的貸款與租賃組合，包括商業與工業貸款、租賃、美國政府擔保貸款與不動產貸款，使我們能有效管理信用風險，並把握更多貸款機會。我們持續透過聘請來自大型銀行的經驗豐富貸款團隊，提升產品與貸款能力。
以下圖表說明我們截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日的貸款與租賃及存款組成：
我們參與特定合併或收購交易的能力，取決於多種因素，包括市場機會、資金取得、銀行監管機構當時對資本水平的觀點、管理層的品質與我們整體財務狀況，以及他們對其他因素的評估，包括我們對法律與法規的遵循情況。自我們 2013 年重組以來，我們已成功完成多項戰略收購，包括：
Oak Park River Forest Bankshares, Inc. 2018
Ridgestone Financial Services, Inc. 2014 Baytree Leasing Company LLC

2025年4月1日，我們完成對First Security Bancorp, Inc.（"First Security Bancorp"），一間德拉瓦州公司，以及First Security Bancorp全資擁有之銀行子公司First Security Trust and Savings Bank（"First Security"），一間伊利諾州發行之銀行（合稱"First Security收購"或"收購First Security"）的收購。請參閱本文件Part II, Item 8, Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements內之Note 3—Acquisition of a Business。
我們主要營運市場為芝加哥都會區，而我們在該地區的44家分行網路為我們的核心通路。我們善用我們聚焦的業務範圍與深厚的關係網路，以提供多元產品為目標，服務當地客戶。
我們的本地分行網路使我們能夠收集低成本存款，推廣Byline品牌與客戶忠誠度，發放貸款、租賃及其他產品，並透過定期參與社區活動維繫與客戶的關係。我們認為，我們的分行網路對我們實現符合公司文化之成功客戶拓展能力至關重要，該文化促進我們與客戶的高互動與主動解決方案。
雖然我們的分行網路仍為我們主要的服務通路，我們瞭解銀行業環境的變化需要數位互動以符合客戶需求。我們持續進行分行網路與現有銀行業務範圍的戰略評估。隨著技術改善與客戶銀行偏好改變，我們定期評估分行擴張與合併潛力，包括客戶使用率、分行獲利能力、所提供的服務、服務市場與與其他據點的距離。
自2013年6月我們重資本化以來，我們的分行網路已從88家減少至45家，包括24家透過收購增加的分行。2025年，一家分行關閉並合併至現有分行據點，且一家租賃分行據點作為First Security收購的一部分被接管，並在收購後關閉。

paragraphs: 本公司營運成果 substantially 取決於淨利息收入，淨利息收入為利息收入與利息支出的差額，其中利息收入主要來自貸款及租賃應收款項的利息收入，包括貸款的累計收入、投資證券及其他短期投資的利息收入，利息支出則主要來自存款與借款。本公司營運成果亦取決於非利息收入的產生，非利息收入主要來自存款的費用及服務費收入、貸款服務收入、財富管理與信託收入、ATM 與交換費收入，以及投資證券與貸款銷售的淨收益。其他影響本公司營運成果的因素包括信貸損失提列、所得稅提列，以及非利息費用，如薪資與員工福利、營運空間與設備費用、資料處理費用及其他雜項營運費用。
本公司於 2025 年的財務狀況、營運成果與流動性受到創紀錄的營收影響，該營收由貸款與租賃組合的成長及存款支付利率降低所驅動，加上本公司收購 First Security，以及為持續強化資產負債表所採取的行動。

本公司於 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年報告合併淨收入為 130.1 百萬美元，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日財年淨收入 120.8 百萬美元增加 9.3 百萬美元，或 7.7%。淨收入增加係因淨利息收入增加 37.3 百萬美元，以及非利息收入增加 2.1 百萬美元，抵銷非利息費用增加 18.1 百萬美元、信貸損失提列增加 9.1 百萬美元，以及所得稅提列增加 2.9 百萬美元。於 2025 年 12 月 31 日及 2024 年 12 月 31 日財年，本公司基本每股盈餘為 2.90 美元與 2.78 美元，稀釋每股盈餘為 2.89 美元與 2.75 美元。於 2025 年 12 月 31 日及 2024 年 12 月 31 日財年，本公司平均資產年回報率為 1.36% 與 1.31%，平均股東權益年回報率為 10.86% 與 11.61%。

截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，總資產為 9.7 十億美元，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日的 9.5 十億美元增加 156.1 百萬美元，或 1.6%。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，總存款為 7.6 十億美元，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日的 7.5 十億美元增加 188.8 百萬美元，或 2.5%。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，總借款及其他負債為 737.3 百萬美元，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日的 946.4 百萬美元減少 209.1 百萬美元，或 22.1%。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，總股東權益為 1.3 十億美元，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日的 1.1 十億美元增加 176.4 百萬美元，或 16.2%。於 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年及 2024 年 12 月 31 日財年，宣佈發放普通股股息為 18.2 百萬美元及 15.9 百萬美元，實際發放普通股股息為 18.2 百萬美元及 15.8 百萬美元。

headings: 與本公司業務相關的風險
本公司業務取決於我們成功管理信貸風險的能力。
我們可能低估貸款及租賃組閤中內含的信貸損失，並產生超過我們為貸款及租賃損失所提列金額的信貸損失。
本公司業務面臨利率風險，利率波動可能對我們的獲利產生不利影響。
我們依賴關於客戶及交易對手之資訊的準確性與完整性。
我們所持有的金融工具價值可能在未來下降。
流動性不足可能影響營運並危及本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果。
本公司流動性取決於 Byline Bank 的股息。
本公司未來可能需要籌集額外資金，而此資金可能在需要時無法取得或完全無法取得。
本公司可能無法實施成長策略或有效管理成本，導致獲利減少或利潤率下降。
新業務線、產品、產品增強功能或服務及技術可能使本公司面臨額外風險。
本公司業務可能因金融市場狀況及總體經濟狀況而受到不利影響。
本公司業務嚴重依賴所經營之不動產市場，因我們貸款組閤中有一大比例是以不動產為擔保。
我們持續面對科技變革。
人工智慧（AI）及本公司實現並運用AI以向客戶提供新產品與服務之能力，可能帶來競爭風險。
貸款出售之獲利認列及服務資產評價之認列，反映某些假設。
本公司會計估計、風險管理程序及控制措施依賴分析及預測技術與模型及假設，這些假設可能無法準確預測未來事件。
本公司之 goodwill 可能發生減值，可能不利影響本公司營運成果與財務狀況，並可能限制 Byline Bank 支付紅利給本公司之能力，進而造成流動性問題。
本公司能認列遞延所得稅資產之利益，取決於未來現金流量與應稅所得。
由於本公司與本公司之外國國籍股東與 FRB 簽訂之承諾，某些活動受到限制。
FRB 之貨幣政策與規範可能不利影響本公司之業務、財務狀況與營運成果。
本公司受多項法律規範，旨在保護消費者，包括社區再投資法案與公平貸款法，若未遵守這些法律，可能導致多種處罰。
未遵守 USA PATRIOT Act、銀行保密法或其他法律與規範，可能導致本公司被處以罰款或處分。
與隱私權、資訊安全及資料保護相關之規範，可能增加本公司之成本，影響或限制本公司蒐集與使用個人資料之方式，並不利影響本公司之業務機會。
美國總統行政當局對法律、規範與政策之潛在變動存在不確定性，這些變動可能直接影響金融機構與全球經濟。

paragraphs: 本公司管理層認為影響我們的主要風險與不確定性已於下文描述。請謹慎考量這些風險，並配合本文件所包含的所有資訊。任何下列風險，以及我們未預見或目前認為不重要之風險，均可能對本公司業務、財務狀況或營運成果造成重大不利影響。

本公司業務之運作需管理信用風險。作為貸款人，我們面臨借款人無法依約償還貸款與租賃之風險，以及用以擔保貸款與租賃償還之財產（如有）可能不足以確保償還之風險。此外，進行任何貸款與租賃亦伴隨固有風險，包括貸款與租賃償還期間之風險、貸款與租賃評估之風險、經濟與產業條件變動所導致之風險，以及處理個別借款人之風險，包括借款人可能未及時向我們提供其業務資訊，或提供不正確或不完整資訊之風險，以及擔保財產價值之風險。為成功管理信用風險，我們必須，除其他事項外，維持嚴謹與謹慎之貸款與租賃評估標準。若因任何原因放寬這些標準、貸款與租賃評估與監控缺乏紀律與勤勉、無法適時調整政策與程序以應對影響借款人之經濟或其他條件變動，以及貸款與租賃組合之品質，可能會導致違約、拍賣與額外呆帳，並可能迫使我們大幅提高信用損失準備金—貸款與租賃，這些均可能對本公司淨收入造成不利影響。因此，本公司若無法成功管理信用風險，可能對本公司業務、財務狀況或營運成果造成重大不利影響。

貸款與租賃組合之信用品質對本公司獲利有重大影響。我們維持信用損失準備金，此為透過費用負擔所建立之準備金，代表管理層對目前預期信用損失之估計。管理層認為此準備金為應對目前預期損失及貸款與租賃組合內固有風險所必需。準備金之水準反映管理層持續評估特定信用風險、組合品質、擔保財產價值、未計息貸款與租賃之數量、組合內目前預期損失，以及經濟、政治與監管條件。管理層使用來自內部與外部相關資訊，依過去事件、目前條件及合理且可支持之預測來估計準備金水準，此可能增加計算之主觀性。此程序對本公司財務結果與狀況至關重要，需進行困難、主觀且複雜之判斷。根據美國通用會計準則（"GAAP"）之企業合併會計原則，透過後續銀行收購取得之貸款，會以其預期公允價值入賬，並同時記錄與這些貸款相關之信用損失準備金。

雖然我們認為信用損失準備金足以吸收貸款與租賃組閤中目前預期之損失，但可能仍不夠。我們可能因多種原因，如影響借款人的經濟條件變動、新資訊及其他我們無法控制之因素，而遭受遠高於準備金之信用損失。若房地產價值下降或我們市場之經濟條件意外惡化，可能導致未納入現有準備金之額外損失。超過現有準備金之損失將減少我們之淨收入，並可能對本公司業務、財務狀況或營運成果造成重大不利影響。若經濟總體、我們市場或影響個別客戶業務與資產之經濟衰退嚴重，將導致增加之呆帳與提高信用損失準備金之需求。
我們未來可能因銀行監管機構之要求，需進一步增加信用損失準備金以補足準備金。銀行監管機構會定期審查我們之準備金、用以決定準備金水準與非 Performing貸款價值之政策與程序。這些監管機構可能要求我們進一步增加準備金或承認未來之呆帳。此外，未來期間之呆帳若超過準備金，將需要提高準備金水準。
本公司信用損失準備金之增加將導致淨收入減少，並可能減少留存收益與資本，因此對本公司業務、財務狀況與營運成果造成重大不利影響。
